builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
summary: EchoMoE replaces full-precision transmission of hidden states in MoE expert-parallel dispatch and combine collectives with transmission of compressed deltas relative to periodically refreshed reference states from earlier layers. It costs a lightweight retrofit fine-tune (roughly 8,500x fewer tokens than pretraining), modest extra computation for compression, and up to 3.8 percentage points of average benchmark degradation. It can fail when the incremental-update assumption breaks down, causing compressed deltas to lose fidelity, and it delivers no benefit without multi-node expert parallelism, which a single 24 GB GPU deployment does not have.
rationale: The technique targets inter-node expert-parallel communication, a bottleneck that only exists in multi-node MoE deployments beyond the reader's single-GPU infrastructure, so it is worth tracking but not actionable now.

claims.statement: EchoMoE replaces full-precision transmission of hidden states in MoE expert-parallel dispatch and combine collectives with transmission of compressed deltas relative to periodically refreshed reference states from earlier layers. It costs a lightweight retrofit fine-tune (roughly 8,500x fewer tokens than pretraining), modest extra computation for compression, and up to 3.8 percentage points of average benchmark degradation. It can fail when the incremental-update assumption breaks down, causing compressed deltas to lose fidelity, and it delivers no benefit without multi-node expert parallelism, which a single 24 GB GPU deployment does not have.

Reduces inter-node communication volume by 58%, improves throughput by 22.6% in the main setup, and improves inference throughput by up to 2.38x over bandwidth-constrained Ethernet, with average benchmark performance within 3.8 percentage points of baseline.
